source: Ministry of Agriculture training module "ជំនិតកម្មដំណាំខ្នុរសំរាប់កសិកម្ម" (Jackfruit Cultivation Techniques for Agriculture), prepared with participation from the Santisena organization, an elderly people's association, a charitable organization, and the CRS (Catholic Relief Services) agriculture program; content compiled with reference to fruit-tree materials and Prek Leap National School of Agriculture (សាលាជាតិកសិកម្មព្រែកលៀប).
text:
Choosing the location and preparing the germination bed properly is an important factor for getting reliable, healthy sprouting of jackfruit seedlings in large numbers. A good nursery bed site should be: near a water source, on well-drained ground that does not flood, receiving enough sunlight, and on elevated, safe ground.

To prepare the bed, raise the soil to a height of about 2 decimeters (roughly 20 cm), with a width of one meter and a length depending on how much is needed. Break the soil up finely, then expose it to the sun for two to three weeks to kill bacteria and various insects, and to allow weeds/grass to be cleared out. The illustration shows a raised bed about 1 meter wide and roughly 2 dm high, prepared with a hoe near a water source and shelter.
